about: Argus typeface library. Every face was fetched live on 2026-11-24 (Google css2 API, Fontshare v2 css API, or the foundry page for self-hosted faces); axes are only those the fetched CSS confirmed. Faces marked overused are current generated-design defaults, kept so the dealer can avoid them; never deal them. Pairings never join two faces of one classification; a pairing whose display and text are one id is a one-family pairing set at two extremes or two widths. A face with no stylesheet URL (source self-host: files from the foundry) is not dealt unless --self-host is given, because a page cannot load it without the files. Faces whose licence forbids redistribution (the Fontshare ITF Free Font License) carry selfHostOnly: they are referenced by name and official stylesheet URL only, never dealt without --self-host, and Argus never downloads or ships their files. Pairing blurbs describe the type only, never a trade.

pairings.why: Width against book: an expanded grotesque at 125% over an editorial serif whose italic is a second voice.
Tall industrial capitals over a sober text serif.
A hairline Didone masthead over a Swiss neutral: contrast of stroke, not of mood.
One family at two widths: expanded 800 for display, 100% at 400 for text; the mono labels the parts.
A blunt grotesque at 900 over a book serif.
One quirky grotesque throughout, with a precise mono only for prices and codes.
A chunky, friendly serif for names over a calm grotesque for the details.
A sharp mid-wide display over a friendly grotesque of different width and mood.
Engraved contrast for headlines over the most legible humanist for everything that must be read.
A stamped slab for names and headings over a warm humanist for the explanations.
A very wide display for the name over a wide mono for figures and short text.
A Caslon over a Franklin Gothic: an old pairing of serif and gothic.
A sharp italic serif as display over a plain civic grotesque.
A tall news gothic over a classical Garamond.
A display that widens as it gets heavy, over a technical mono for labels and short text.
A soft, cheerful display over a mono for prices, codes and short labels.
A punchy 800 grotesque for the headline over a lively text serif with a real italic.
A one-weight poster display over a light literary serif.
Ultra-tall capitals over an academic old-style: height against roundness.
A brutal condensed for the name, a friendly grotesque so the details stay easy.
A wide rounded display that fills a line, over a quiet grotesque of normal width.
A crisp wedge-serif display over a narrow grotesque.
An elegant italic-led serif display over a clean corporate grotesque.
The new Playfair at large optical size over an old gothic for text; Playfair stays above 60px.
One family at two widths: Archivo expanded 800 for display, normal width 400 for text.
One mechanical family: expanded 900 for display, normal width for text.
One humanist at two widths: condensed 800 for headings, normal for text.
One family, two settings: CASL 1 brush-mono for display, sans for text.
One book serif at two extremes: 900 tight for display, 400 at text size for long reading.
One grotesque at 900 against 400: hierarchy by weight alone, one voice.
Geometric capitals over a bookish old-style.
A geometric display over a sturdy screen slab.
A sign-like condensed for the big words over the most legible humanist for instructions.
A melting display that carries the message, a plain grotesque that carries the facts.
A fat, round display over a warm calligraphic serif.
A puffy, playful display over a rounded text face.
Blocky capitals over a clean geometric for text.
A soft serif display over a calm grotesque.
One Didone at two optical sizes: opsz 96 for display, opsz 11 for text.
A wide geometric display over a document serif, mono only for figures.
A round, airy grotesque over a light literary serif.
